skills.name: average_fiber_size_via_degree
skills.description: For a finite étale morphism π : X → Y of varieties defined over ℤ, the limit of the average size of the fibers over Y(𝔽_p) as p→∞ equals the geometric degree of π.
skills.preconditions: π is finite étale over a dense open subset of Y, and both X and Y are defined over ℤ with well‑defined reductions modulo p for all sufficiently large primes.
skills.postconditions:
The asymptotic average 
\(\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#Y(𝔽_p)}\sum_{y\in Y(𝔽_p)}\#π^{-1}(y)\) is identified with deg(π).
skills.example: Let X⊂A^2 be defined by y^2 = x^3 + x and π(x,y)=x. Over ℤ this map is finite étale away from the discriminant Δ=−4. Its geometric degree is 2, so the average number of solutions to y^2 = x^3 + x modulo p tends to 2 as p→∞.

skills.name: lang_weil_point_estimate
skills.description: Give an estimate for the number of 𝔽_q‑points of a variety V of dimension d and degree D, namely \(\#V(𝔽_q)=q^d+O(q^{d-1/2})\), using the Lang–Weil theorem.
skills.preconditions: V is a geometrically irreducible projective (or affine) variety defined over 𝔽_q, with known dimension d and degree D.
skills.postconditions: An asymptotic formula for \(\#V(𝔽_q)\) with an explicit error term O(q^{d-1/2}) is obtained.
skills.example: For the smooth plane conic C: x^2 + y^2 = 1 in ℙ^2 over 𝔽_q, d=1 and D=2, so \(\#C(𝔽_q)=q+1+O(\sqrt{q})\).

skills.name: chebotarev_density_for_fiber_sizes
skills.description: Use the Chebotarev density theorem to relate the distribution of Frobenius conjugacy classes in the Galois group of a finite cover to the frequencies of different fiber cardinalities over 𝔽_p‑points.
skills.preconditions: A finite Galois cover f : X → Y defined over a number field, with Galois group G, and a description of how each conjugacy class determines the cycle type of the fiber over a rational point.
skills.postconditions: Statistical proportions of each possible fiber size are expressed in terms of the proportion of corresponding conjugacy classes in G.
skills.example: For the cover of the line given by the polynomial t^3‑2, the Galois group is S_3. Chebotarev tells us that over 𝔽_p, the polynomial splits completely (fiber size 3) for 1/6 of the primes, has one linear and one quadratic factor (fiber size 2) for 1/2 of the primes, and remains irreducible (fiber size 1) for 1/3 of the primes.

skills.name: tangency_condition_as_resultant
skills.description: Express the condition that two plane conics C₁ and C₂ are tangent by requiring the discriminant of the intersection polynomial to vanish, equivalently the resultant of their defining quadrics and a linear combination equals zero.
skills.preconditions: Two conics given by homogeneous quadratic forms Q₁(x,y,z) and Q₂(x,y,z) in ℙ^2.
skills.postconditions: A single homogeneous polynomial equation R(Q₁,Q₂)=0 in the coefficients of Q₁ and Q₂, which cuts out the tangency locus in the product of the parameter spaces.
skills.example: If C₁: x^2 + y^2 = z^2 and C₂: ax^2 + by^2 = cz^2, the tangency condition reduces to (a−b)^2 = 4c(a+b), the vanishing of a resultant of the two quadrics.

skills.name: compute_degree_of_projection
skills.description: Determine the degree of a projection map from an incidence variety to a parameter space by counting the number of solutions of the defining equations for a generic point of the target.
skills.preconditions: An incidence variety I⊂X×Y defined by algebraic equations, and the projection π : I→Y is dominant and generically finite.
skills.postconditions: The geometric degree deg(π) is obtained as the number of points in the fiber over a generic y∈Y, often computed by solving a zero‑dimensional system.
skills.example: Let I⊂(ℙ^2)^{*}×ℙ^2 be the set of pairs (ℓ,P) with P∈ℓ. The projection to the dual projective plane has degree 1 because a generic line ℓ meets the plane in exactly one point of the incidence variety.

skills.name: generic_finiteness_and_etaleness_criterion
skills.description: Apply the Jacobian (or differential) criterion to a morphism to identify a dense open subset of the target over which the map is finite and étale.
skills.preconditions: A morphism f : X→Y of varieties over a field, with X and Y smooth, and the relative dimension of X over Y is zero at generic points.
skills.postconditions: An explicit open subset U⊂Y where the Jacobian matrix has full rank, guaranteeing that f|_{f^{-1}(U)} is finite étale.
skills.example: For the map π: ℙ^1×ℙ^1 → ℙ^1 given by (s,t)↦s^2+t^2, the Jacobian determinant 2s·2t is non‑zero away from the coordinate axes, so π is étale over the complement of {s=0}∪{t=0}.

skills.name: grothendieck_ltrace_point_count
skills.description: Use the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula to express the number of 𝔽_q‑points of a variety as an alternating sum of traces of Frobenius on its ℓ‑adic cohomology groups.
skills.preconditions: A separated scheme X of finite type over 𝔽_q, and a prime ℓ≠char 𝔽_q.
skills.example: For X=ℙ^1 over 𝔽_q, the only non‑zero compactly supported cohomology groups are H^0_c≅ℚ_ℓ and H^2_c≅ℚ_ℓ(-1); the trace formula gives \(\#ℙ^1(𝔽_q)=q+1\).

skills.name: determine_monodromy_group
skills.description: Compute the monodromy (Galois) group of a family of covers by analyzing how loops in the base permute the points in a generic fiber, often showing it is the full symmetric group.
skills.preconditions: A dominant, generically finite morphism f : X→Y with X irreducible and Y smooth, and a description of the branch locus.
skills.postconditions: Identification of the monodromy group G⊂S_n (n=deg f), which can be used to infer uniformity of fiber sizes and transitivity properties.
skills.example: For the cover of the line given by y^n = x(x-1), the monodromy group is the full cyclic group ℤ/nℤ acting transitively on the n sheets.

skills.name: bertini_smoothness_for_parameter_spaces
skills.description: Apply Bertini’s theorem to guarantee that a general member of a linear system (e.g., a conic) is smooth, thereby defining a dense open subset of the parameter space.
skills.preconditions: A linear system of divisors on a smooth projective variety, and a base field that is infinite (or sufficiently large finite).
skills.postconditions: Existence of a non‑empty Zariski open subset U of the parameter space such that every point corresponds to a smooth divisor.
skills.example: In the projective space ℙ^5 parametrizing plane conics, the discriminant hypersurface Δ⊂ℙ^5 cuts out singular conics; its complement U=ℙ^5\Δ is the open set of smooth conics.

skills.name: inclusion_exclusion_to_remove_degenerate_fibers
skills.description: Use the principle of inclusion–exclusion to subtract contributions from fibers where the morphism fails to be étale (e.g., where tangency conditions become degenerate).
skills.preconditions: A finite morphism π : X→Y with a known closed subset D⊂Y where π is not étale, and point‑count formulas for both X and π^{-1}(D).
skills.postconditions: An adjusted count \(\#π^{-1}(Y\setminus D)(𝔽_q)=\#X(𝔽_q)-\#π^{-1}(D)(𝔽_q)\), leading to a refined average fiber size.
skills.example: For the map π: A^1→A^1 given by t↦t^2, the branch point 0 is degenerate. Over 𝔽_p, \#π^{-1}(𝔽_p)=p, and \#π^{-1}(0)=1, so after exclusion the average over non‑branch points is (p‑1)/ (p‑1)=1, matching the degree away from the branch.
